text.p: Hansabank-Latvija said on Thursday that it has applied for central bank approval to raise its statutory capital to six million lats, a rise of 1.5 million lats.

"The bank has applied to the central bank for permission to boost the statutary capital to six million lats by 1.5 million lats," Valdis Purvinskis, Hansabank-Latvija's deputy board chairman, told a news conference.
"We are planning to reach a 20 percent return on capital this year which would give us a 1997 after-tax profit of one million lats," Purvinskis said.
The bank also said that its profit for the first four months of the year came to 450,000 lats against a first quarter profit of 300,000 lats.
Its balance sheet total came to 67 million lats at the end of April against 55.59 million lats at the end of March, Purvinskis said.
"The board expected a much more painful transition back into profit when planning the 1997 budget," Purvinskis said.
The bank registered a 1996 loss of 422,725 lats and its balance sheet total for the year was 63.22 million lats.
